svg.text: ESP32 solar tracker: wiring as built (demo, adapter-powered)
8 panels (4S2P) · INA219 + ACS712 · 4 LDRs · photo transistor · DHT11 · DS18B20 · 2 × MG996R · 2-ch relay · 2 × LM2596 · 12 V 2 A adapter
POWER PATH (thick wires for the panel and 12 V lines)

g.text: VIN: Buck A 5 V, or USB power (never both)
4 LDRs as two parallel pairs (east → GPIO 34, west → GPIO 35)
Each pair reads as one sensor. A shade wall separates east from west.
Mount flat beside the panels, outside the wiper's path
Tilt servo MG996R: sun / torch tracking
5 V rail (Buck A), or USB power
INA219, DHT11, DS18B20, LDRs, photo tr.
✓ Every GPIO used once; no boot/strapping or flash pins
✓ All analog inputs on ADC1 (33, 34, 35, 36, 39): they work with Wi-Fi on
✓ No pin sees more than 3.3 V (ACS712 and 12 V go through dividers)
✓ Only one I²C device (INA219 0x40): no address clash
✓ Panels → ACS712 → INA219 in series: both sensors see the same current
✓ Panel current goes only into the 4.4 Ω load, never onto the +12 V bus
✓ 5 V rail and servo rail are separate; only the grounds are joined
✓ Relays switch only + wires; one common ground everywhere
! Both servos share Buck B: the firmware never moves them together
Same label = same wire, e.g. LDR-E at the LDRs goes
Set both bucks BEFORE connecting anything to them.
Power-up: ESP32 USB first, then the adapter.
